headline: Australia's medicines and devices regulator says eight of 12 AI note-taking tools for doctors may count as medical devices, even though none of their makers registered them as such.
score_reason: Regulator finding with direct effect on a fast-growing product class; the review did not test safety.
importance_line: Doctors and patients in Australia use these tools in consultations, and tools that go beyond transcription may now need registration, but the regulator has not named the eight products or found any breach of the law.
summary: Medical Republic reports that Australia's Therapeutic Goods Administration reviewed 12 digital scribe products, some of them the best-known, and found eight have functions likely to qualify as medical devices, because newer AI features can draw clinical conclusions or recommendations rather than only transcribe. The regulator stressed that it did not test safety or performance, and said disclaimers saying a product is not a medical device are not enough.
notes: TGA has not said which eight products; Medical Republic asked and had no reply by deadline.
